summary:
Worked the Identity management lane on shop.lab.test (HTTP only) read-only; no test accounts and writes disabled, so POST flows were observed but not exercised.

Reachable identity surfaces: /login, /register, /forgot-password, /admin/ (401 Admin Login), and API /api/v1/username-available.

Findings per item:
- IDNT-01 Role definitions (done): Two roles observed (customer vs admin, admin boundary at /admin/ -> 401). The /register form carries a client-controlled hidden field role=customer -> mass-assignment/privilege-escalation candidate. Recorded as HIGH lead; could not confirm server-side trust because writes are disabled.
- IDNT-02 Registration (done): Open self-service registration at /register; password minlength=4 only (weak), no CAPTCHA/email-verification visible, uses username-availability API.
- IDNT-03 Provisioning (done): Fully self-service, unauthenticated, no approval/confirmation step; account role supplied by client.
- IDNT-04 Enumeration (done): /api/v1/username-available is an unauthenticated yes/no oracle — username=alice returns available:false (exists) vs admin/test/support/random available:true. Recorded as MEDIUM lead. Forgot-password form also submits username via GET (username leaked in URL/logs) — recorded as LOW lead; its action was not probed.
- IDNT-05 Username policy (done): Weak/unenforced — reserved name "admin" available, case-sensitive (ADMIN distinct), no whitespace trim ("admin " distinct), no pattern/length constraint on the form.

Not tested: actual registration POST (including role=admin mass-assignment), forgot-password reset-link behavior, and GraphQL queries — all require writes/POST that this read-only lane does not permit. A person should validate the mass-assignment lead via an approved write.
